25	## Capability Name: Camera-layout and articulated occlusion reasoning
26	**Applicable Conditions:** A large object, doorway, furniture, or wall has the wrong silhouette, depth order, or visibility.
27	**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** An edge-on face, intervening wall, incorrect hinge, or camera projection can each hide the same object. Image evidence includes visible contour, floor occlusion, wall junctions, semantic orientation, and neighboring landmarks; it does not identify the hidden room. 
28	**Executable Method:** `spatial.project_points(scene, camera, points)` returns normalized camera projections and camera-space depth, using Blender's world-to-camera projection. `spatial.hinge_positions(hinge, width, angles, local_direction)` provides candidate free-edge locations in world XY. Specify radians and world units. Build a leaf and its details as children of a pivot at the jamb; the opening must be an actual opening, not a dark patch over solid wall. Compare swings at fixed camera first; then if necessary vary camera pose and focal length together with room dimensions. Rank reference landmarks, visible face width, relative scale, edges and occlusion, not one contour alone. Keep furniture positions coherent and parent leaf details to the hinge.
29	**Verification Method:** Render camera comparisons with identical lighting; temporarily hide only the suspected wall, then restore it. Inspect top and side views of *the selected* assembly, including the full swing arc, hinge to jamb alignment, opening, walls, furniture, and floor. Check projected points for positive camera depth and inspect clipping. Validate after any camera or layout revision.
30	**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Projection ignores occlusion and lens distortion; hinge helper assumes a vertical axis. Better visible leaf width alone does not justify a displaced hinge or a leaf wider than its opening. Isolated or obstructed views cannot prove absence of intersections. Single-view matching can compromise other landmarks.
31	**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** General projective geometry and articulation prior; historical door trials in both repetitions motivate visibility isolation and candidate comparison. One selected case had an obstructed side diagnostic, so coherence was not established; do not treat that placement as a repair recipe. Details in research evidence.
32	
33	## Capability Name: Material mapping versus illumination experiment
34	**Applicable Conditions:** A surface appears too uniform, too streaky, or wrongly oriented.
35	**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Surface color, roughness, illumination, and geometry can produce similar marks. Coordinate choice and object scale change the apparent direction and wavelength; diffuse variation should remain attached to the surface when the light moves, while specular highlights can move.
36	**Executable Method:** `appearance.directional_stone(name, scale, colors, roughness, distortion)` creates an editable procedural Blender material using object coordinates, axis scaling, a noise texture and a color ramp; returns the material. Scale is a three-vector in local coordinate units, and colors are linear RGBA. Assign explicitly to the intended material slot. Adjust scale/axes for streak direction; apply or account for object transforms. For another candidate use an independently authored UV/image mapping with appropriate color space and packing, and a roughness-only candidate. Compare all under identical camera, exposure, geometry and render settings, then move a light independently. Do not assume object coordinates are meters after object scaling; seams and texture direction on edges need inspection.
37	**Verification Method:** Compare reference-aligned crops and full-frame renders for spatial frequency, contrast, coverage, edge continuity, orientation and neighboring brightness; compare each candidate under both light directions. Use neutral light and color management consistently. Record what moved and what did not; change one factor at a time.
38	**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** A procedural node network or image texture is not evidence of improvement. Highlights and indirect light also depend on roughness, geometry and camera; light tests do not uniquely decompose appearance. Object-space mapping may distort on nonuniform scale; image coordinates may stretch or clamp on edges.
39	**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Both historical material runs rendered color, image and roughness candidates under alternate lighting and retained image candidates. Procedural implementation here is an independently written general hypothesis, not their selected texture or a proven transfer.

41	## Capability Name: Support and assembly diagnostics
42	**Applicable Conditions:** An object may float, penetrate a support, or disconnect after a repair.
43	**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Bounding boxes conflate support with proximity and do not show true contact. An assembly can be connected internally yet float, or rest on a floor while components are disconnected.
44	**Executable Method:** `support.sample_support(obj, supports, tolerance, band, ray_margin)` samples evaluated mesh vertices in a low-Z band, casting vertically from above each sample onto the supplied evaluated mesh supports. Returns per-sample signed vertical gaps and a conservative category. World Z is up; supports must be explicitly supplied. A negative gap is only *possible* penetration. Missing rays yield unknown; near-zero is not proof of physical contact. `support.world_bounds(obj)` provides evaluated bounds for broad-phase checking only. Move a complete assembly or redesign its feet as separate candidates rather than blindly snapping individual parts.
45	**Verification Method:** Inspect all feet/wheels, full sample coverage, local supports, side views, clearance, and changed silhouette; repeat after the selected repair. Separately inspect joints (wheel/fork, fork/spoke, post/seat), including top/side views and evaluated geometry. Use denser surface sampling or mesh intersection testing for critical results; rays and vertices alone can miss intersections, overhangs, or unsupported areas.
46	**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Downward ray tests assume an appropriate horizontal support and do not establish stability, exact contact, connectivity, or volume intersection. The highest hit can be a top surface above the object; ray margin must exceed geometry thickness. Modifiers and sparse meshes affect sampling. Unknown is not a pass.
47	**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Historical chair runs compared whole-chair lowering against caster changes with evaluated wheel samples and side views. Their numerical checks are sampled estimates, not a physics proof; prior knowledge supplies the interpretation boundaries.

import bpy


def directional_stone(name, scale=(3.0, 0.7, 1.0),
                      colors=((0.6, 0.61, 0.6, 1), (0.9, 0.9, 0.89, 1)),
                      roughness=0.45, distortion=0.3):
    if len(scale) != 3 or len(colors) != 2:
        raise ValueError('scale needs three components and colors two RGBA values')
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
